topic.title: Multimodal AI Systems: Vision, Audio and Video

outcomes: Normalize image/document OCR regions while preserving page, bounding box, reading order and confidence.
Preserve table structure, transcript timestamps, speaker labels and video frame timecodes through processing.
Align audio segments and sampled video frames with explicit temporal tolerances and missing-evidence behavior.
Build modality-aware evidence records and citations with stable source, page/region or time provenance.
Apply tenant, user and group ACLs before multimodal retrieval ranking and abstain on low-confidence evidence.
Evaluate OCR/ASR quality with CER/WER and measure temporal alignment, citation provenance and modality-specific failure rates.

Stage 10 tenant isolation and prompt-injection trust boundaries
Stage 12 Topic 3 advanced retrieval and Topic 4 evaluation

glossary.definition: Optical character recognition converts text visible in images or scanned documents into machine-readable text and regions.
A document extraction method that preserves relationships among text blocks, columns, headings, tables and page coordinates.
Word error rate measures insertions, deletions and substitutions in a recognized transcript relative to a reference.
Character error rate measures character-level insertions, deletions and substitutions relative to reference text.
The process of identifying which speaker produced each segment of an audio recording.
A mapping between transcript segments and video frames or events using timestamps and an explicit tolerance.
Linking a model's description or answer to a specific image region, page location or frame rather than an unsupported summary.
Metadata that identifies the source asset, version, page/region or timestamp and transformation lineage for a retrieved claim.
A calibrated or estimated quality signal whose meaning depends on the OCR, ASR, vision or alignment component that produced it.
Retrieval over evidence from multiple modalities while preserving authorization, modality and source-level citation information.

explanation.problem: Enterprise knowledge is not only text. Contracts arrive as scanned PDFs with columns and tables; meetings contain audio with speakers and timestamps; product walkthroughs contain video frames; and images may embed instructions or sensitive data. Flattening all of this into plain text loses layout, temporal alignment, confidence and source provenance. A plausible answer can then cite the wrong page, speaker or frame—or cross an authorization boundary.
explanation.plainLanguage:
Treat each media asset as a source with a stable ID, version, tenant and retention policy. Use modality-specific adapters: OCR for scanned pages, layout parsing for headings and tables, ASR for speech segments, diarization for speaker labels, and frame sampling for video. The local lab uses pre-extracted synthetic outputs so you can study the evidence pipeline without needing a hosted model or GPU.

For documents, preserve page number and bounding box for every OCR block. Reading order is not always the order in which text appears in a raw extraction: columns, footnotes and tables need layout-aware reconstruction. Keep table rows and columns explicit rather than joining all cells into one sentence. Preserve the original region and confidence so uncertain OCR is not silently promoted to fact.

For audio, store transcript segments with start/end milliseconds, speaker ID and confidence. Do not replace the original offsets with a re-chunked transcript index. For video, sample frames using a declared policy and retain exact timestamps. Align a transcript segment to the nearest frame only when the temporal distance is within a configured tolerance; otherwise preserve an unaligned segment.

Normalize all outputs into evidence spans. Each span should carry modality, source asset/version, tenant, ACL, confidence, text or structured payload, and page/region or time coordinates. Retrieval must filter tenant and user/group ACLs before scoring and top-k. Parent or adjacent evidence needs its own authorization check. A citation must preserve the source location: page and bounding box for documents, time range and speaker for audio, frame timestamp for video.

Low-confidence evidence should be excluded or shown as uncertain, not treated as a fact. If no authorized evidence survives the threshold, abstain. Content extracted from a document, image, audio track or video frame is untrusted data; it may contain prompt injection, but it cannot grant tool authority or rewrite system policy.

Evaluate each modality separately. OCR CER and ASR WER measure recognition errors but do not prove semantic correctness. Measure table cell accuracy, reading-order accuracy, diarization, timestamp alignment, frame coverage, citation correctness and retrieval quality by language, document type, audio quality and modality. Preserve the original asset and transformation versions so errors can be reproduced.
explanation.mentalModel: Media asset → modality adapter → normalized regions/segments/frames → confidence and provenance → tenant/ACL filtering → multimodal retrieval → context and location-aware citations → grounded answer or abstention.
limitations: The local pipeline consumes synthetic OCR/ASR/frame outputs; it does not measure a real OCR, ASR or vision model.
Simple y/x OCR ordering does not solve complex multi-column, rotated, handwritten or nested-table layouts.
Nearest-frame alignment is a baseline and does not establish semantic synchronization or speaker-to-face identity.
WER/CER do not measure meaning, factual correctness, layout accuracy or downstream answer quality.
Confidence scores are not automatically calibrated across modalities or providers.
Media can contain prompt injection, malware, PII or copyrighted content; ingestion needs separate security, consent and retention controls.
A source citation with coordinates proves traceability metadata, not that the model interpreted the region correctly.
explanation.everydayAnalogy: A journalist does not cite only the transcript of a press conference. They retain the recording timestamp, speaker, video frame and document page that supports each statement. Multimodal AI needs the same evidence trail so a reader can verify where a claim came from.
explanation.mathMadeSimple: If a transcript reference has 100 words and ASR produces 8 insertions, 5 deletions and 7 substitutions, WER = (8+5+7)/100 = 0.20 or 20%. This measures recognition error, not whether the resulting answer is factually correct.
explanation.productionImpact: Version each modality adapter and source asset; preserve OCR boxes, table structure, transcript offsets, speaker IDs and video timestamps; enforce ACLs before retrieval; calibrate confidence by modality; retain provenance through compression and citations; and abstain when evidence is uncertain or unauthorized.

useCase.scenario: An enterprise assistant answers a policy question using a scanned PDF, a recorded meeting and a training video. The response must cite the exact PDF page/region and audio/video time, avoid low-confidence OCR, respect tenant and user ACLs, and treat embedded media instructions as untrusted evidence.
actors: Video frame sampler and temporal aligner
inputs: Scanned pages with OCR blocks and bounding boxes
Tables with explicit rows and columns
Audio transcript segments with start/end and speaker
Tenant/user/group ACL and modality confidence thresholds
constraints: Page, region, timestamp, speaker and source version are preserved.
Low-confidence evidence cannot satisfy answer thresholds.
Tenant and ACL filters execute before ranking.
Transcript/frame alignment must meet configured tolerance.
Untrusted media text cannot grant tool authority.
Missing or unauthorized evidence causes abstention.
useCase.successMetric: Every returned citation points to a reproducible source location; unauthorized and low-confidence evidence is excluded; unaligned media remains explicitly unaligned; no-evidence queries abstain.

trustBoundaries: Original media and all extracted text are untrusted data.
Extraction model outputs are uncertain and modality-specific.
Tenant/user/group identity comes from verified server context.
Every derived span retains source asset and ACL lineage.
Citations are evidence references, not instructions or tool permissions.
failurePaths: OCR reading order is wrong: preserve raw regions and compare layout-aware reconstruction.
Table is flattened: keep row/column cell structure and source boxes.
ASR confidence is low: abstain or request human review rather than invent words.
Timestamp alignment exceeds tolerance: leave frame_id unset and retain transcript time.
Cross-tenant evidence matches strongly: exclude before ranking and cache lookup.
Media contains prompt injection: label as untrusted content and keep policy/authorization separate.
Citation loses source coordinates: block answer publication until provenance is restored.

workedExample.input: PDF page 2 region [20,30,400,90] says 'Retention period is thirty days' at confidence 0.99; audio segment 1200–3200 ms says the same with speaker-1 at confidence 0.91.

steps.reasoning: Keep page, bounding box and confidence; sort blocks by page and reading order.
steps.result: document evidence at page 2 with exact region and 0.99 confidence

steps.reasoning: Keep original start/end milliseconds, speaker ID and ASR confidence.
steps.result: audio evidence at 1200–3200 ms for speaker-1

steps.reasoning: Filter by tenant and user/group ACL before scoring either modality.
steps.result: only authorized PDF and audio spans remain

steps.reasoning: Citations carry the PDF region and audio timestamp rather than a generic file link.

failures.name: OCR reading order and layout loss
failures.symptom: Columns, footnotes or table cells appear in the wrong sequence.
failures.rootCause: Text is flattened without page coordinates or layout-aware reconstruction.
failures.recovery: Preserve raw regions, sort using layout metadata and keep table structure explicit.
failures.regressionTest: Provide out-of-order OCR blocks and assert page/region order and table cells remain intact.

failures.name: Low-confidence OCR or ASR
failures.symptom: An uncertain recognition is presented as a confident fact.
failures.rootCause: Confidence is dropped or thresholds are not modality-specific.
failures.recovery: Preserve confidence and exclude uncertain evidence or route it to human review.
failures.regressionTest: Query only a low-confidence span and assert the system abstains at the configured threshold.

failures.name: Transcript timestamp drift
failures.symptom: A citation points to the wrong part of a meeting recording.
failures.rootCause: Original segment offsets are discarded during chunking or normalization.
failures.recovery: Retain source start/end milliseconds and transformation lineage.
failures.regressionTest: Assert normalized transcript segments preserve exact offsets and speaker IDs.

failures.name: Video frame misalignment
failures.symptom: A transcript is cited with an unrelated frame.
failures.rootCause: Nearest frame is selected without a maximum temporal tolerance.
failures.recovery: Use a declared sampling interval and leave the frame unaligned when outside tolerance.
failures.regressionTest: Use a distant frame and assert frame_id is null.

failures.name: Cross-tenant multimodal retrieval
failures.symptom: A high-scoring image, transcript or document from another tenant is returned.
failures.rootCause: Authorization is applied after ranking or omitted from a modality index.
failures.recovery: Push tenant/user/group ACL filters into candidate generation before ranking.
failures.regressionTest: Add a stronger cross-tenant matching span and assert it never enters the candidate set.

failures.name: Prompt injection embedded in media
failures.symptom: OCR or ASR text attempts to override policy or request a tool call.
failures.rootCause: Extracted media text is treated as trusted instruction.
failures.recovery: Keep all extracted text in an untrusted evidence channel and authorize tools independently.
failures.regressionTest: Insert instruction-like content into a synthetic image/transcript and prove it cannot grant authority.

failures.name: Citation provenance loss
failures.symptom: Answer cites a file but not the page, region, timestamp or speaker that supports it.
failures.rootCause: Metadata is dropped during retrieval, compression or answer assembly.
failures.recovery: Require provenance fields on every selected evidence span and citation.
failures.regressionTest: Reject citation construction when required source location metadata is missing.

scenarioQuiz.question: Why must OCR blocks retain page and bounding-box metadata?
options: To preserve reading order and reproducible source-region citations
scenarioQuiz.explanation: Page and region metadata preserve layout and allow a reader to verify which exact source region supports the answer.

scenarioQuiz.question: What should happen when a transcript segment is outside the video-frame alignment tolerance?
options: Attach the nearest frame regardless of distance
Leave the segment unaligned and preserve its original time range
scenarioQuiz.explanation: A forced alignment creates false provenance. Keep the timestamp and leave frame_id unset when no frame is sufficiently close.

scenarioQuiz.question: Which metric measures word-level ASR recognition errors?
scenarioQuiz.explanation: WER measures word insertions, deletions and substitutions. It does not alone measure semantic or factual correctness.

scenarioQuiz.question: A cross-tenant image has the highest lexical match. When should it be filtered?
scenarioQuiz.explanation: Tenant and ACL filtering must happen before ranking so unauthorized evidence never enters the candidate set or cache.
